events.name: MUSEUM PRINT SHOP: CHILDREN’S Hand Press
events.excerpt: “I often think that the night is more alive and colourful than the day.” – A quote from Vincent van Gogh serves as our inspiration this autumn at the KINDERhandPRESSE in the FHXB’s historic print works.

events.name: Unterscheidet euch!
events.address: Parkaue 29 THEATER AN DER PARKAUE, 10367 Berlin

events.name: Die fabelhaften Millibillies
events.excerpt: Emilia has dreamed up an entire band: drums, guitar, keyboard, and bass. And suddenly, a boy from her class shows up—Tobi—and he just won’t disappear from her dream!

events.name: Sleeping Beauty
events.address: Oranienburger Straße 32 In den Heckmann Höfen, 10117 Berlin

events.name: Aschenputtel - Interactive Theater

events.name: aneinander-vorbei
events.excerpt: A musical game about 1,000 wishes and unforgettable moments Theater for the little ones. Two actors and a musician playfully and associatively improvise a story about the exciting encounters between children and adults that happen during a…

events.name: The Spooky Schusch
events.excerpt: On the lonely Dogglspitz mountain live the stubborn deer, the shy chicken, the nasty chamois, the grumpy marmot, and the party-loving rabbit.

events.name: The History of Nutrition
events.excerpt: No more chocolate crises. Candy debates. Cookie conflicts! Parents and caregivers are all too familiar with the discussion about (un)healthy eating.

events.name: Hansel and Gretel: Interactive Theatre | Domäne Dahlem
events.address: Oranienburger Straße 32 In den Heckmann Höfen, 10117 Berlin
events.excerpt: Much to their stepmother’s delight, Hansel and Gretel get lost in the forest. Driven by hunger, they find their way to the witch’s cottage. The witch captures them.

events.name: Guided tour for families
events.excerpt: When was the Komische Oper Berlin founded? What’s the story behind the “komische” name? And what does it actually look like behind the curtain at the Schillertheater?

events.name: Family morning
events.excerpt: During the Berlin Christmas vacations, children and their families have the opportunity to take a look behind the scenes of the Staatsballett Berlin.

events.name: It's the Turtle's Birthday
events.excerpt: It’s the turtle’s birthday. What she’d love most is a head of lettuce—big, green, and juicy. I wonder if anyone will think of that? The lion comes by and gives her a piece of meat; the elephant brings her a bucket of water.

events.name: Hans im Glück
events.excerpt: As a reward for seven years of service, Hans receives a large lump of gold from his master. For Hans, it’s now time to set out into the world, into life, and into freedom.

events.name: Pippi Longstocking

events.excerpt: ‘Ahoy and away!’ Pippi Longstocking is moving into the Villa Villekulla. She plans to wait for her father there, a captain who went missing during their last adventure together on the high seas.

events.name: KLING KLANG
events.excerpt: Does a ‘Klang’ sound or does a ‘Klong’ ring? Does a ‘Dang’ warble or does a ‘Song’ toot? Does a ‘Tut’ sing or does a ‘Träller’ dang? Does a ‘Bing’ bong or does a ‘Kling’ clang?

events.name: Vier zurück
events.excerpt: One, two, three and four are back! One and Two are there for each other and do everything together. But Three doesn't join in. He says: “No, I can do it alone.” And dives under the table!

events.name: Das NEINhorn
events.excerpt: Director Birga Ipsen stages the cult bestseller by Marc-Uwe Kling for children aged 4 and up.

events.name: Das tapfere Schneiderlein Mitspieltheater I Dahlem
events.excerpt: Interactive theater is a special form of theater in which an experienced actress tells a fairy tale while taking on the various fairy-tale characters and roles.

events.name: Der kleine Muck
events.address: Oranienburger Straße 32 In den Heckmann Höfen, 10117 Berlin
events.excerpt: The shrewd Muck enters the service of a sorceress and discovers a pair of magic slippers that enable him to travel from place to place in the blink of an eye.

events.name: Bach. Das Leben eines Musikers. (Kurzversion)
events.excerpt: The biographically influenced production with chamber orchestra and choir brings the life and work of the important composer to the stage.

events.name: No Planet B
events.excerpt: Three young people imagine that a climate catastrophe has struck, and they are sitting in the International Children’s Court.

events.name: Krach & Keks
events.excerpt: "Krach & Keks" is a play about growing up in times of change – and the power to reinvent oneself without losing everything.

events.name: The Century of Displacement
events.excerpt: Why do people have to flee or are expelled? What do they experience? The Documentation Centre for Displacement, Expulsion, Reconciliation looks at politically, ethnically and religiously motivated forced migrations in the 20th century in…

events.name: The Bremen Town Musicians - play along theater

events.name: The Second Princess, or How to Become the First
events.excerpt: Once upon a time, there were two princesses—the first and the second, the big one and the little one. The first princess liked being first—but the second princess didn’t like being second.

events.name: Open printing workshop
events.excerpt: Want to print pictures like a real artist? Kurt Mühlenhaupt created art for children. At the museum, you can create your own art with lots of color, creativity, and fun.

events.name: Try it!

events.name: Wedding Market

events.excerpt: Once a month, the Bibliothek am Wasserturm invites babies aged 0 to 3, accompanied by a parent, grandparent or childminder, to a special morning in our children’s library.

events.excerpt: Everything you want to know about the GDR!

events.excerpt: At the Computer Games Museum, experience the virtual worlds of today, as well as the games from your own youth and those of your parents and grandparents.

events.excerpt: Hey Wind, you cheerful fellow! You ruffle and roar, things flutter and storm, blowing hats off heads and leaves and apples from the trees.

events.name: 37. BERLINER MÄRCHENTAGE (37th BERLIN FAIRY TALE DAYS)
events.excerpt: From 5 to 22 November 2026, the world’s largest fairy-tale festival will bring a host of dazzling experiences to the grey days of November with its rich programme of events, which this year is dedicated to music in fairy tales and stories.

events.name: The Three Little Pigs
events.excerpt: The three little pigs, Willi, Billi and Zilli, come face to face with the big bad wolf. But with wit, courage and teamwork, they won’t be fooled so easily!

events.name: Wusel und seine Freunde – Theater Katinchen
events.excerpt: Wusel is once again indulging in his favourite pastime: searching for things. On his way, he meets his friends, who love playing with him. In the process, they forget something important, and suddenly it’s not so much fun anymore.

events.name: ElternzeitKultur - Taking the baby to the museum
events.excerpt: During ElternzeitKultur, you can explore BERLIN GLOBAL with your baby. A live speaker will provide exciting background information in individual short tours.

events.name: Bookworms: Story time for children
events.excerpt: You’re invited to the ‘Lesemäuse’ storytelling session every Thursday at 4.30 pm (except during school holidays)!

events.name: Picture Book Cinema in the Afternoon
events.excerpt: Every Thursday, nursery children are invited to the picture book cinema. Together, they immerse themselves in a variety of stories – some funny, some thrilling, and some really exciting.

events.name: 16GB: Table Tennis Table Policy
events.excerpt: Ever chilled out on a ping-pong table? On the ping-pong table in Andaç and Ceren’s neighborhood, people party, laugh, and argue.

events.name: Baby on board – turn on the sound!
events.excerpt: At the (Grand)parents and Babies Sing-Along, we sing, rock, clap and listen. Familiar and new songs are combined with simple rhythm games, movement and babies’ first sounds.

events.name: It’s Teddy Schnuff’s birthday
events.excerpt: It’s Teddy Schnuff’s birthday – and Toni is busy getting everything ready! But between the balloons, the presents and a mum who’s constantly getting in the way, things aren’t going quite to plan.

events.name: Top-class sailing up close: the Capital Sailing Cup
events.excerpt: When some of the best sailors compete on the water, the Wannsee becomes the stage for thrilling top-class sport: from 6 to 8 November 2026, the Capital Sailing Cup will take place at the Seglerhaus am Wannsee sailing club (VSaW).

events.name: Lantern Workshop
events.excerpt: Under the guidance of a local artist, children can make their very own lanterns.

events.name: Torch light Tour
events.excerpt: Once the museum doors have closed, you’ll sneak through the dark museum rooms by the light of your torches. As you search for the various nocturnal animals, you’ll explore the museum’s exhibitions.

events.name: With a flashlight to the electress
events.excerpt: I wonder if the castle is haunted once it gets dark in the evening? Young visitors and their parents will find out on this extraordinary guided tour.

events.name: Stories Left Untold
events.excerpt: In *Tales Not Told*, the string quartet Anadolu Quartet Europe, together with illustrator Ernesto Herrera Ortez and singer and intercultural moderator Gamze Karaca, tells the stories of musicians and peoples who have been persecuted,…

events.name: Award Ceremony for the Berlin Play Prize for Young Audiences
events.address: Parkaue 29 THEATER AN DER PARKAUE, 10367 Berlin
events.excerpt: On November 6, 2026, the Berlin Play Award for Young Audiences will be presented for the second time at the Theater an der Parkaue; the State of Berlin uses this award to honor outstanding plays for children and young people.

events.name: SHROUDED
events.excerpt: Through impressive trio acrobatics, “SHROUDED” explores the power of human emotions and translates the complexity of inner states into movement. Inner turmoil stands alongside moments of harmony and lightness.

events.name: Animated Film Saturday
events.venue: Deutsche Kinemathek - Museum für Film und Fernsehen
events.excerpt: Point your mobile phone camera at something – that always works. But how do you make an animated film? It’s easy to learn!

events.name: Bauhaus Lab: Let the Dolls Dance!
events.excerpt: From 1920 onwards, Oskar Schlemmer headed the sculpture class at the Bauhaus. He wanted to create the image of a new kind of human being. You take his ‘figurines’ as your model and create simplified, clear figures using geometric shapes.

events.name: Halloween concerts for babies and children at Spandau Citadel
events.excerpt: Babyevents Berlin organises concerts for babies, toddlers and their families in the Gothic Hall at Spandau Citadel.

events.name: BERLIN GLOBAL Stories from Berlin and the world - Public family tour in German language
events.excerpt: Whizzing through BERLIN GLOBAL: Each room promises a new view of Berlin and the world, shared ideas and fun!

events.name: LICHTenberg – The Light Orchestra
events.excerpt: Discover immersive light art and electronic music across two extraordinary swimming halls in Berlin’s historic Stadtbad Lichtenberg.

events.name: LICHTenberg – The Light Orchestra
events.excerpt: Discover immersive light art and electronic music across two extraordinary swimming halls in Berlin’s historic Stadtbad Lichtenberg.

events.name: Is it all just a film?
events.excerpt: Experience how images and music come together at a silent film concert, or watch drawings take shape live before your very eyes during a script reading.

events.name: LICHTenberg – Light, Sound & Atmosphere
events.excerpt: 100 years of history meets light art – the imposing architecture of the historic municipal swimming pool is transformed into a vibrant stage through dynamic light and sound.

events.name: Family Concert – Halloween Special!
events.excerpt: The Family Concert – Halloween Special! at Spandau Citadel invites families to enjoy a musical experience in an autumnal atmosphere.

events.name: HUMBOLDT LABORATORY - On Water. Guided family tour in German language
events.excerpt: What does it sound like when a tree drinks? How are people around the world coping with increasing drought? What does a puddle researcher do? And how do you study water on Mars?

events.name: The Eyelash Gnomes
events.excerpt: When Charlotte tries to fall asleep, there are lions roaring at her, or lifts flying up into the clouds, and the planet of eyes that are always open. So she’d rather stay awake, make a racket and play at the circus!

events.name: WaterCreatures Creative. Workshop for families
events.excerpt: Jellyfish, whales, penguins and boxfish: many fascinating animals live on, in and under water. Some of them are featured in the science exhibition ‘On Water’.

events.name: Ach so! Neue Musik einfach verstehen
events.excerpt: The luck of the dice and the magic of sound. Chance made its way into composition with New Music. Inspired by John Cage, children aged 5 and over discover this world through play.

events.name: The Wizard of Oz
events.excerpt: A modern adaptation of the classic musical. When Dorothy finds herself in the Land of Oz, she sets off to find the Wizard of Oz.

events.name: Bauchgefühl
events.excerpt: Two people with different ways of perceiving the world keep bumping into each other in an office. One rainy day, the adventure takes its course: suddenly, objects come to life, words turn into movement, gestures into sound, and images into…

events.name: Surprise! The circus is here!
events.venue: Kinder und Familientheater Coq Au Vin (Neukölln)
events.excerpt: Helmut the elephant has disappeared! And of all times, right before the show is about to begin. The clumsy detective Jonathan takes on the investigation and finds himself unwittingly caught up in the whirlwind of circus life.

events.name: Wusel and the Red Secret – Theater Katinchen
events.excerpt: In the first instalment of the trilogy, Wusel, the little troll, scurries through the forest. He’s an expert at finding things and stumbles across all sorts of interesting things.

events.name: St Martin’s Day
events.excerpt: By the light of the lanterns, everyone makes their way through the pre-winter open-air museum. As dusk falls, young and old gather in the village square. Together, they hear the story of Saint Martin and the beggar.

events.name: Is the castle haunted?
events.excerpt: When night falls in Königs Wusterhausen, once the visitors and the castle staff have long since gone home, the adventure tour through the ‘Soldier King’s’ hunting lodge begins.

events.name: Flash Light Tour for Children
events.excerpt: On the torch-lit tour at the Haus am Waldsee, you’ll explore Peter Wächtler’s artworks in an unusual light. Who’s that emerging from the darkness?

events.name: Mini Movers Club – Kids’ Yoga
events.excerpt: Mini Movers Yoga is all about discovery: as they journey through colourful fantasy worlds, children explore what their bodies are capable of.

events.name: 20th Textile Day
events.excerpt: On the 20th Textile Day, numerous artists will be showcasing their work and running mini-workshops where visitors can try out various techniques.

events.name: Family Concert: THE LITTLE MAGIC FLUTE
events.excerpt: An original, child-friendly, lively, and humorous version of the most famous opera of all time!

events.name: Friedenau is dancing! Big open day at the Keller Dance School
events.excerpt: On Sunday, 8 November 2026, things will be hopping at Rheinstraße 44: the Keller Dance School will be opening its doors from 11 am to 5 pm and inviting children, teenagers and adults to a varied day full of music, movement and the joy of…

events.name: The furious kitchen circus
events.excerpt: Two chefs invite you to the table! There's apple pie! The two clowns create their little kitchen world with imagination and humor, which exudes charm and magic.

events.name: Wusel und das freche Flämmchen
events.excerpt: Do you actually know where Wusel lives? Well, in his underground cave, of course! Do you like nut cake as much as we do? Wusel bakes it for the princess with the help of Tilly the squirrel.

events.name: Fabric for Change! Sustainable Sewing Hub
events.excerpt: In this open workshop, you can bring textiles and old clothes to repair, alter, or create something new. Be inspired by the exhibitions, themes, and exhibits in the building—and strike up conversations with others while sewing, mending,…

events.name: Family Sunday: Wer spricht denn da?
events.excerpt: Talking bears, cunning foxes and rowing moles – in Peter Wächtler’s works, the audience encounters animals, mythical creatures and fairy-tale characters.

events.name: Ancient picture stories in 3D
events.excerpt: Explore the Pergamon Frieze, which tells of the battle of the Olympian goddesses against the giants. Decipher the dramatic scenes. Pose yourself.

events.name: Creative Kids Berlin Workshop: Art made from leaves and foliage
events.excerpt: Leaves become art: at the Creative Kids Berlin workshop at Manifesto Market Berlin, children aged 5 and over can create their own leaf-print picture and take it home with them.

events.name: Krieg der Knöpfe
events.address: Schifffahrtsufer 2 an der Dischinger Brücke, 13581 Berlin-Spandau
events.excerpt: In two villages that had been at loggerheads for ages, even the children had always been at each other’s throats, and because at some point they started cutting off their opponents’ buttons, their war came to be known as the ‘War of the…

events.name: Shadow theatre
events.excerpt: This year, the Berlin Fairy Tale Days are being held under the theme “The Magic Flute and the Star Harp – Music in Fairy Tales and Stories”.

events.name: Fender, makeup case, and lots and lots of Christmas cookies
events.excerpt: Alina is a theater artist. With her suitcase full of makeup, she reinvents herself every day. But sometimes she wishes there was someone who would like her just the way she really is.

events.name: For children only
events.excerpt: Renowned for their commitment to offering children and parents original, high-quality music, 3Berlin have become a fixture on the German-speaking children’s music scene.

events.name: Moby Dick
events.excerpt: Imagine there were no cats. And no dogs. There are no guinea pigs and no goldfish, no canaries and no horses. No bark beetles, no grass mites, no tigers, no whales and no dinosaurs. Oh, right, they’ve been gone for a while now.

events.name: Sterntaler
events.address: Oranienburger Straße 32 In den Heckmann Höfen, 10117 Berlin
events.excerpt: A girl gives everything she has until she has nothing left, and then a miracle happens: she receives more than she can carry.

events.name: A Berlin Winter’s Tale
events.excerpt: With the audience’s help, Babette Winter reads the fairy tale of Little Moritz — accompanied by Mühlenhaupt’s illustrations and the barrel organ.
